In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.﴾

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was traveling with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on one of his journeys. Umar asked him about something, but he did not answer him. He asked again, and he did not answer him. He asked a third time, and he did not answer him. Umar said: "May your mother be bereft of you, O Umar! You have pressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) three times, and each time he has not answered you." Umar said: "So I urged my camel forward and went ahead of the people, and I feared that some Qur'an would be revealed concerning me. Before long I heard a crier calling out to me, so I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and greeted him, and he said: 'Tonight there was revealed to me a surah that is dearer to me than everything the sun rises upon,' then he recited: 'Indeed, We have given you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of Hudaybiyah: 7/452. "Nazzarta" means: you pressed/insisted.]]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Umar Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, grandson of al-Abbas ibn Hamzah, related to us, al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali related to us, Affan related to us, Hammam related to us, Qatadah related to us, Anas related to us, who said: "The verse, 'Indeed, We have given you a clear victory,' down to the end of the verse, was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) on his return from Hudaybiyah, while his companions were overcome by sorrow and distress. He said: 'A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the whole world.' When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) recited it, a man from the people said: 'Congratulations and good cheer to you, O Messenger of Allah! Allah has made clear what He will do with you, so what will He do with us?' Then Allah revealed the next verse: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, until He concluded the verse." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of Hudaybiyah: 7/450-451; by Muslim in al-Jihad, chapter on the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, no. (1786): 3/1413; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/222.]]

They differed concerning this victory. It was narrated from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Qatadah, from Anas, that it is the conquest of Makkah. Mujahid said it is the conquest of Khaybar. [[In al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/508, from Anas.]]

The majority hold that it is the Treaty of Hudaybiyah. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/89.]]

The meaning of fath (victory/opening) is the opening of what was closed. The treaty with the polytheists at Hudaybiyah had seemed impossible until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, opened it. Shu'bah related from Qatadah, from Anas, concerning "Indeed, We have given you a clear victory," that he said: "Hudaybiyah."

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "You count the victory as the conquest of Makkah, and indeed the conquest of Makkah was a victory. But we count the victory as the Pledge of Ridwan on the day of Hudaybiyah. We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) fourteen hundred men, and Hudaybiyah was a well. We drained it, and we did not leave in it a single drop. The news reached the Prophet (ﷺ), so he came to it and sat on its edge, then he called for a vessel of water, performed ablution, rinsed his mouth, made supplication, and poured it into the well. We left it for a short while, then it gave us water sufficient for ourselves and our mounts." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of Hudaybiyah: 7/441.]]

al-Sha'bi said concerning His words, "Indeed, We have given you a clear victory": it is the victory of Hudaybiyah, by which he was forgiven his earlier and later sins; and they were fed the palm trees of Khaybar; the offering reached its place of sacrifice; and the Romans prevailed over the Persians, so the believers rejoiced at the ascendancy of the People of the Book over the Magians. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/89; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/510.]]

al-Zuhri said: "There was no victory greater than the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, for the polytheists mingled with the Muslims and heard their speech, so Islam took firm root in their hearts, and within three years a great multitude embraced Islam and the ranks of Islam were greatly increased." [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/89; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/510.]]

His words, Mighty and Majestic: "Indeed, We have given you a clear victory" mean: We have decreed for you a manifest decree. Al-Dahhak said: "Indeed, We have given you a clear victory" without fighting, and the treaty was among the forms of victory.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verse 2:

It has been said: the lam in His words ﴿that He may forgive﴾ is the lam of purpose (lam kay), meaning: "We have granted you a manifest victory so that there may be combined for you, along with forgiveness, the complete favor in the conquest."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it refers back to His words: "And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women" [Muhammad: 19], "that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what follows," and "that He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens..." up to the end of the verse.

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: it refers back to His words: "When there comes the help of Allah and the victory, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt [Allah] with the praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness" (al-Nasr: 1-3), "that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah), before the prophethood, and what follows" up to the time of the revelation of this surah. [[See: al-Tabari: 26/68.]]

It has also been said: ﴿and what follows﴾ refers to what will happen, and this is according to the view of those who permit minor sins (saghair) upon the prophets. [[Al-Qurtubi said: 1/308-309 "The scholars differed on this matter: did minor sins occur from the prophets, for which they are held to account and reproached, or not? Having agreed that they are protected from major sins and from every vile trait that carries blemish or deficiency, by consensus according to al-Qadi Abu Bakr, and according to al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq that this is required by the evidence of the miracle, and according to the Mu'tazilah that this is required by the evidence of reason on their principles. Al-Tabari and other jurists, theologians and traditionists said: minor sins do occur from them. This is in contrast to the Rafidah, who said that they are protected from all of that, and they argued by what occurred of such in the revelation and what is established of their disavowal of it in the hadith, and this is clear and not hidden. The majority of jurists from the companions of Malik, Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i said: they are protected from all minor sins just as they are protected from all major sins, because we were commanded to follow them in their deeds, traces and conduct with an absolute command without any restricting indication. So if we permitted minor sins upon them, it would not be possible to emulate them, since not every one of their actions has a distinguished intent of worship, permissibility, prohibition or disobedience, and it is not valid that a person be commanded to comply with an order which may be a sin, especially for those among the usulis who give precedence to action over speech when they conflict. Al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Isfara'ini said: they differed about minor sins, and what the majority hold is that this is not permissible for them; some went to permitting them, but this view has no basis. One of the later scholars who held the first view said: what should be said is that Allah the Exalted has informed of the occurrence of sins from some of them, attributed them to them, reproached them for them; and they informed of them about themselves, disavowed them, feared them and repented. All of that came in many places that do not accept interpretation as a whole, even if individual instances may accept it, and all of that does not diminish their rank. Those matters which occurred from them were rare, by way of error and forgetfulness, or an interpretation that led to it; so relative to others they are good deeds, but relative to them they are faults compared with their ranks and the height of their stations, since the minister may be held to account for what the administrator is rewarded for. So they feared that on the Day of Standing, while knowing of their security, safety and peace. He said: this is the truth. Al-Junayd spoke well when he said: "The good deeds of the righteous are the faults of those brought near." Concerning them, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them, although the texts testify that sins occurred from them, that did not impair their rank nor detract from their standing; rather Allah has rectified them, chosen them, guided them, praised them, purified them, selected them and favoured them, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them.]]

Sufyan al-Thawri said: ﴿what preceded﴾ refers to what you did in the time of ignorance, and ﴿what follows﴾ is everything you did not do; and such is mentioned by way of emphasis, as it is said: "He gave to whoever saw him and whoever did not see him, and struck whoever met him and whoever did not meet him."

Ata al-Khurasani said: ﴿what preceded of your sin﴾ means the sin of your two parents, Adam and Eve, by your blessing; and ﴿what follows﴾ means the sins of your community through your supplication. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 16/263.]]

﴿And complete His favor upon you﴾ by prophethood and wisdom, ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾, i.e., keep you firm upon it. The meaning is that there may be combined for you, along with the conquest, the complete favor through forgiveness and guidance to the straight path, which is Islam. It has also been said: "and guide you" means "guide through you."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verse 3–4:

﴿And that Allah may help you with a mighty help﴾ — ghaliban (overpowering). It was also said: mu'izzan (granting might).

﴿It is He who sent down tranquility﴾ — al-tuma'nina (serenity) and al-waqar (dignity), ﴿into the hearts of the believers﴾ — so that their souls would not be disturbed by what befalls them. Ibn 'Abbas said: every sakinah (tranquility) in the Qur'an means tuma'nina, except the one in Surat al-Baqarah, ﴿that they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah sent His Messenger with the testimony that there is no god but Allah. When they affirmed it, He added to them the prayer, then the zakat, then the fasting, then the Hajj, then the jihad, until He perfected their religion for them [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/72. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/514) added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]]. So whenever they were commanded with something and they affirmed it, they increased in affirmation upon their affirmation.

Al-Dahhak said: certainty along with their certainty.

Al-Kalbi said: this refers to the matter of al-Hudaybiyah, when Allah made true to His Messenger the vision with truth.

﴿And to Allah belongs the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾.

﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and remove from them their misdeeds; and that is with Allah a great triumph.﴾ It has been mentioned from Anas that when ﴿That Allah may forgive you﴾ was revealed, the Companions said: "Congratulations and good tidings! ﴿And He will punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾: the people of hypocrisy in Medina and the people of polytheism in Mecca. ﴿Who assume about Allah an assumption of evil﴾: that He would not give victory to Muhammad and the believers. ﴿Upon them is a cycle of evil﴾: with punishment and destruction. ﴿And Allah has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil is it as a destination.﴾

﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise. Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good tidings and a warner, that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and support him﴾, meaning help him and aid him, ﴿and honor him﴾, meaning venerate him and exalt him. These pronoun references return to the Prophet ﷺ, and here is a pause. ﴿And exalt Him﴾, meaning exalt Allah, that is, pray to Him, ﴿morning and evening﴾, meaning at dawn and at dusk. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "liyu'minu" (that they may believe), "wa-yu'azziruhu," "wa-yuwaqqiruhu," and "wa-yusabbihuhu" with the yā' (ya) in all of them, in accordance with His words "in the hearts of the believers." The others recited them with the tā' (ta).

[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the recommendation of the Imam taking the pledge of his army when he intends to fight, and the Pledge of Good Pleasure under the tree, no. 1856: 3/1483.]]

Al-Suddi said: They used to take hold of the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledge allegiance to him, and the hand of Allah is over their hands in the pledge.

Al-Kalbi said: The blessing of Allah upon them in guidance is above what they did in the pledge. [[See al-Qurtubi: 26/267.]]

﴿Our wealth and our families have kept us busy﴾, meaning the women and the offspring (dharari, sg. durriyyah), that is, there was no one to take our place with them. ﴿So ask forgiveness for us﴾ for our staying behind you. So Allah the Exalted refuted them in their excuse, and said:

﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾, concerning the matter of asking forgiveness, for they do not care whether the Prophet ﷺ asks forgiveness for them or not.

﴿Say: "Who then can avail you anything against Allah if He intends harm for you, or intends benefit for you"﴾ [suwa'an (harm)] [[زيادة من "ب".]]. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿ضُرًّا﴾ with a damma on the ḍad, while the others read it with a fatḥa, because it is paired with ﴿نَفْعًا﴾ (benefit), and al-Naf' is the opposite of al-ḍarr (harm). [Page 129/b.] They had supposed that their staying behind the Prophet ﷺ would ward off harm from them and hasten benefit to them through safety in their persons and their wealth. So He informed them that if He intended any of that for them, no one could avert it.

﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verses 15–16:

﴿The ones who stayed behind will say﴾: meaning those who stayed behind from al-Hudaybiyah. ﴿When you set out﴾: that is, when you go and depart [O believers] [[Addition from "B".]], ﴿to take spoils, [saying,] "Let us follow you"﴾: meaning the spoils of Khaybar. ﴿Let us follow you﴾ to Khaybar, "so that we may witness the fighting against its people with you." This is because, when they returned from al-Hudaybiyah, Allah promised them the conquest of Khaybar and made its spoils exclusively for those who had witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, as compensation for the spoils of the people of Makkah, which they had not obtained, since they had withdrawn from them under a truce and had gained nothing from them.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "كَلِمَ اللَّهِ" (kalima Allah), without an alif, as the plural of "kalimah" (word). The others recited "كَلَامَ اللَّهِ" (kalam Allah, the speech of Allah). The meaning is that they wish to alter Allah's promises to the people of al-Hudaybiyah, namely that Khaybar's spoils belong to them exclusively.

Muqatil said: it means the command of Allah to His Prophet (ﷺ) that none of them should set out with him.

Ibn Zayd said: it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "So if they ask your permission to go out, say: 'You will never go out with me, ever.'" [al-Tawbah: 83]. The first view is more correct, and it is the view of the majority of the people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir).

﴿Say: "You will not follow us"﴾ to Khaybar. ﴿Thus has Allah said before﴾: that is, before our return to you, that the spoils of Khaybar belong to those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and that others have no share in them. ﴿They will say, "Rather, you envy us"﴾: that is, envy prevents you from letting us share the spoils with you. ﴿Rather, they did not understand﴾: they did not know about Allah what religious matters were for them and against them. ﴿except a few﴾ among them, and that understanding was from the truthfulness of Allah and His Messenger.

﴿Say to the ones who stayed behind of the Bedouins: "You will be called to a people of great military might"﴾. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and [Ata'] [[Omitted from "A".]] said: they are the people of Persia. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/82; Ibn Kathir: 4/191; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519 also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]] Ka'b said: they are the Romans. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; see also Ibn Kathir: 4/191.]] al-Hasan said: Persia and the Romans. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/82; Ibn Kathir: 4/191; al-Suyuti also attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519 to Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Hawazin and Thaqif. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; see al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519.]] Qatadah said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; Ibn Kathir: 4/191; Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/226.]] al-Zuhri, Muqatil, and a group said: they are Banu Hanifah, the people of al-Yamamah, the companions of Musaylimah the Liar. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519 also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani.]]

Rafi' ibn Khadij said: "We used to recite this verse without knowing who they were, until Abu Bakr called for fighting Banu Hanifah, and then we knew that they were them." [[See al-Qurtubi: 16/272.]]

Ibn Juraij said: "Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) called them to fight Persia."

Abu Hurayrah said: "This verse has not yet come." [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83, who said by way of preference: "The most correct view on this matter is to say that Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed us that these Bedouins who stayed behind will be called to fight a people of might in battle and valor in wars, and He did not clarify for us, by any report or by reason, that the intended ones are Hawazin, nor Banu Hanifah, nor Persia, nor the Romans, nor specific individuals. It is permissible that He meant some of these groups, and permissible that He meant others. The most correct statement on it is to say as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: they will be called to a people of great might."]]

﴿Say: "You will not follow us"﴾ to Khaybar. ﴿Thus has Allah said before﴾: that is, before our return to you, that the spoils of Khaybar belong to those who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah, and that others have no share in them. ﴿They will say, "Rather, you envy us"﴾: that is, envy prevents you from letting us share the spoils with you. ﴿Rather, they did not understand﴾: they did not know about Allah what religious matters were for them and against them. ﴿except a few﴾ among them, and that understanding was from the truthfulness of Allah and His Messenger.

﴿Say to the ones who stayed behind of the Bedouins: "You will be called to a people of great military might"﴾. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and [Ata'] [[Omitted from "A".]] said: they are the people of Persia. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/82; Ibn Kathir: 4/191; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519 also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]] Ka'b said: they are the Romans. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; see also Ibn Kathir: 4/191.]] al-Hasan said: Persia and the Romans. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/82; Ibn Kathir: 4/191; al-Suyuti also attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519 to Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Hawazin and Thaqif. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; see al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519.]] Qatadah said: Hawazin and Ghatafan on the day of Hunayn. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; Ibn Kathir: 4/191; Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir: 2/226.]] al-Zuhri, Muqatil, and a group said: they are Banu Hanifah, the people of al-Yamamah, the companions of Musaylimah the Liar. [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/519 also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani.]]

Rafi' ibn Khadij said: "We used to recite this verse without knowing who they were, until Abu Bakr called for fighting Banu Hanifah, and then we knew that they were them." [[See al-Qurtubi: 16/272.]]

Ibn Juraij said: "Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) called them to fight Persia."

Abu Hurayrah said: "This verse has not yet come." [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 26/83, who said by way of preference: "The most correct view on this matter is to say that Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed us that these Bedouins who stayed behind will be called to fight a people of might in battle and valor in wars, and He did not clarify for us, by any report or by reason, that the intended ones are Hawazin, nor Banu Hanifah, nor Persia, nor the Romans, nor specific individuals. It is permissible that He meant some of these groups, and permissible that He meant others. The most correct statement on it is to say as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: they will be called to a people of great might."]]

﴿You will fight them, or they will submit. So if you obey, Allah will give you a good reward﴾: meaning Paradise. ﴿But if you turn away [and refuse] [[Addition from "B".]] as you turned away before﴾: that is, on the occasion of al-Hudaybiyah, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾: which is the Fire. When this verse was revealed, the people of disability (ahl al-zamanah, those with chronic illness or incapacity) said: "What about us, O Messenger of Allah?"

Then Allah the Exalted revealed [see al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/521]: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ [meaning, in staying behind from jihad] [addition from "b"], ﴿and whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away, He will punish him with a painful punishment﴾.

The reciters of Madinah and Syria read "nudkhilhu" (ﷺ-less, "We will admit him") and "nu'adhdhibhu" ("We will punish him") with the nun in both places, while the others read them with the ya' (yudkhilhu, yu'adhdhibhu), in accordance with His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you﴾ at al-Hudaybiyah, on the condition that they would fight the Quraysh and not flee, ﴿under the tree﴾. It was a samurah (the samurah, with a dammed mim, is a type of acacia tree, a large tree of the 'idah (thorny trees) category). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: My father told me that he was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under the tree. He said: When we left the following year, we forgot it and could not locate it. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of al-Hudaybiyah: 7/447.]

It is also narrated that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by that place after the tree had gone, and said: Where was it? Some of them began to say: Here; and others: Here. When their disagreement increased, he said: Move on, the tree has gone. [See: al-Tabari: 26/87.]

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Na'imi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us; 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, saying, 'Amr said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us on the day of al-Hudaybiyah: "You are the best people on earth." We were one thousand four hundred. And had I been able to see today, I would have shown you the place of the tree. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of al-Hudaybiyah: 7/443, and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the Imam's pledge to the army when they intend to fight, no. (1856): 3/1484; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/195.]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us; 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj; Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to us; Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir being asked: How many were there on the day of al-Hudaybiyah? He said: We were fourteen hundred, and we pledged allegiance to him while 'Umar was holding his hand under the tree, and it was a samurah. We pledged to him, except Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari, who hid under the belly of his camel. [Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the recommendation of the Imam's pledge to the army when they intend to fight, no. (1856): 3/1483.]

And Salim narrated from Jabir, who said: We were fifteen hundred. [A fragment of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of al-Hudaybiyah: 7/441.]

'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa said: The companions of the tree were one thousand three hundred, and Aslam were an eighth of the Muhajirun. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of al-Hudaybiyah: 7/443, and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the recommendation of the Imam's pledge to the army when they intend to fight, no. (1857): 3/1485.]

The cause of this pledge, as mentioned by Muhammad ibn Ishaq from the people of knowledge, was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Khirash ibn Abi Umayyah al-Khuza'i when he camped at al-Hudaybiyah, and sent him to the Quraysh in Makkah, mounting him on his camel called al-Tha'lab, to convey to their nobles what he had come for. They hamstrung the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) camel and wanted to kill him, but the Ahabish protected him, and they released him until he reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned 'Umar ibn al-Khattab to send him to Makkah. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I fear the Quraysh for myself, and there is no one from Bani 'Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah who would protect me, and the Quraysh know my enmity toward them and my harshness against them. But I will direct you to a man who is more honored among them than I am: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned 'Uthman and sent him to Abu Sufyan and the nobles of the Quraysh, to inform them that he had not come for war, but had come only as a visitor to this House, to honor its sanctity. 'Uthman set out for Makkah, and Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As met him when he entered Makkah, or before he entered it. He dismounted from his mount, carried him before himself, then seated him behind him, and gave him protection until he conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the leaders of the Quraysh heard that 'Uthman had finished the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they said to him: If you wish to circumambulate the House, then do so. He said: I will not do that until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) circumambulates it. So the Quraysh detained him with them. Then word reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims that 'Uthman had been killed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We will not depart until we fight these people," and he called the people to the pledge, and so it was the Pledge of Ridwan under the tree.

The people used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge from them to death. Bakr ibn al-Ashajj said: They pledged to him to death, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, to what you are able."

Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah and Ma'qil ibn Yasar said: We did not pledge to him to death, but we pledged to him that we would not flee. The first to pledge in the Pledge of Ridwan was a man from Bani Asad called Abu Sinan ibn Wahb. No one among the Muslims who attended it stayed away except Jadd ibn Qays, of Bani Salamah. Jabir said: It is as if I am looking at him, pressed against the armpit of his she-camel, hiding himself from the people. Then news reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that what had been mentioned about 'Uthman was false. [Narrated by Ibn Ishaq: 2/314-316. See also: al-Albani's annotation on "Fiqh al-Sirah" by al-Ghazali, p. (342).]

Abu Sa'id al-Shirihi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me; 'Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Nadrawayh narrated to us; Abu 'Imran Musa ibn Sahl ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Jawni narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us; al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "None of those who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah, chapter: On the Caliphs: 7/31; al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib, chapter: What has come concerning the virtue of those who pledged under the tree: 10/362, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir: 2/310; and Imam Ahmad: 3/350. And Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Jabir, from Umm Mubashshir, that she heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say in the presence of Hafsah: "None of the companions of the tree, those who pledged under it, will enter the Fire, God willing." ... and he mentioned the story of Hafsah bint 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with her). See: Sahih Muslim, Book of the Virtues of the Companions, chapter: On the virtues of the companions of the tree, no. (2496): 4/1942.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So He knew what was in their hearts﴾ of sincerity and loyalty, ﴿and sent down tranquility upon them﴾, meaning calm and contentment, ﴿and rewarded them with an imminent victory﴾, meaning the conquest of Khaybar.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verses 19–20 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿And many spoils that they will take﴾ from the properties of the Jews of Khaybar. Khaybar had land and property, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided them among them. ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾.

﴿Allah has promised you many spoils that you will take﴾: these are the conquests that will be opened for them until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So He hastened this for you﴾, meaning Khaybar, ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾. This is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) headed for Khaybar and besieged its people, some tribes of Banu Asad and Ghatafan intended to raid the dependants and children of the Muslims in Madinah. So Allah restrained their hands by casting terror into their hearts. It was also said: "He restrained the hands of the people from you", meaning the people of Makkah, through the treaty. ﴿And that it may be a sign for the believers﴾, concerning the truthfulness of you [the Prophet], ﴿and that they may know that Allah is the One who protects and guards them, in their presence and in their absence﴾, ﴿and guides you to a straight path﴾: He will keep you firm upon Islam and increase you in insight and certainty through the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Khaybar. This is because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyah, he remained in Madinah for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah and part of Muharram. Then he set out in the latter part of Muharram of the seventh year (AH) towards Khaybar.

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, who said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) : whenever he raided a people with us, he would not attack us until morning and would look. If he heard the adhan, he would refrain from them; and if he did not hear the adhan, he would attack them. He said: So we set out for Khaybar and reached them at night. When it was morning and he did not hear the adhan, he mounted, and I mounted behind Abu Talhah, and my foot was touching the foot of the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: So they came out to us with their baskets and their shovels. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ), they said: "Muhammad, by Allah, Muhammad and the army!" When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them, he said: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Khaybar is ruined! Indeed, when we descend into the courtyard of a people, the morning of those who were warned is evil." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter: What blood is protected by the adhan: 2/89-90; Muslim in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter on the Battle of Khaybar, no. (1365): 3/1426-1427; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/58-59.]]

We were informed by Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir, who said: we were informed by Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, who said: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, who said: Abu Ali al-Hanafi Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Majid informed us, who said: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, who said: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to me, saying: ... We set out to Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: My uncle Amir began chanting verses to the people:

"By Allah, were it not for Allah, we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity or prayed.
And we are not free from Your bounty, so make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy].
And send down tranquillity upon us."

[The words within the brackets are an addition from manuscript "b".]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am Amir." He said: "May your Lord forgive you." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never asked forgiveness for a person in particular except that he was martyred. He said: Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, who was on his camel, called out: "O Prophet of Allah, if only you had let us enjoy Amir!" He said: When we arrived at Khaybar, their king Marhab came out swaggering with his sword, saying: "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab, armed and a tested champion, when wars approach, blazing." [The word "Khaybar" is missing from manuscript "a".]

He said: Then my uncle Amir came out to face him and said: "Khaybar knows that I am Amir, armed and a daring champion." He said: They exchanged two blows. Marhab's sword struck the shield of Amir, and Amir went to strike from below, but his sword turned back upon himself and severed his artery, and that was the cause of his death. Salamah said: I went out and found a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) [manuscript "b" page 130] saying: "The deed of Amir has come to nothing; he killed himself." He said: So I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) weeping and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the deed of Amir has come to nothing; he killed himself." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who said that?" I said: "Some people among your companions." He said: "The one who said that has lied; rather, he will have his reward twice." Then he sent me to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who had an eye infection, and said: "I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." He said: So I went to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and brought him, leading him by the hand while he had an eye infection, until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He spat into his eyes and they were healed, and he gave him the banner. Marhab came out saying: "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab, armed and a tested champion, when wars approach, blazing."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I am the one whom my mother named Haydar, like a lion of thickets, of fearsome appearance. I give them full measure with the sa', like the measuring of the sandara." [In manuscript "b": "severe, a lion" (shadid qaswarah).]

He said: So he struck the head of Marhab and killed him. Then the conquest came at his hands. [[Narrated by Muslim in extended form in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter on the Battle of Dhi Qarad, no. (1807): 3/1433-1441; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/19-22.]]

The account of Khaybar was narrated by a group: Sahl ibn Sa'd, Anas, and Abu Hurayrah, who add and omit [details from one another]. In it: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been seized by a severe headache (al-shaqiqah) and did not go out to the people. So Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) took the banner of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then advanced and fought a fierce battle, then returned. Then Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) took it and fought a fierce battle, more severe than the first, then returned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of this and said: "Tomorrow I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love; Allah will grant the conquest at his hands." He called Ali ibn Abi Talib and gave it to him, and said: "Go, and do not turn around until Allah grants you victory." So he came to the city of Khaybar, and Marhab, the lord of the fortress, came out wearing a helmet and a stone with a hole in it like a helmet upon his head, reciting verses. Ali came out to face him and struck him, splitting the stone and the helmet and cleaving his head until the sword reached the molars. Then after Marhab, his brother Yasir came out reciting verses, and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam came out against him. His mother Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib said: "Will my son be killed, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Rather, your son will kill him, if Allah wills." Then they met, and al-Zubayr killed him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to conquer the fortresses, to kill the fighting men, to take the children captive, and to seize the wealth.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first of their fortresses to be conquered was the fortress of Na'im, and there Mahmud ibn Maslamah was killed; the Jews threw a stone at him and killed him. Then [the Muslims] conquered al-'Amus, the fortress of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq, and obtained captives from it, among them Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. Bilal brought her and another woman with her, and he passed by them over the corpses of Jewish men slain. When the woman with Safiyyah saw them, she screamed, struck her face, and threw dust upon her head. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Take this she-devil away from me," and he ordered Safiyyah to be brought and placed behind him, and he threw his cloak over her. The Muslims knew that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had chosen her for himself. The Messenger of Allah said to Bilal, when he had seen what he had seen from that Jewish woman: "Has mercy been removed from you, O Bilal, that you pass by two women over the corpses of their men?" Safiyyah had seen in a dream, while she was a bride of Kinanah ibn al-Rabi' ibn Abi al-Huqayq, that a moon had fallen into her lap. She related her dream to her husband, and he said: "This is nothing but that you desire the king of Hijaz, Muhammad." He struck her face, and her eye turned green from it. She was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a mark from it, and he asked her what it was. She informed him of this account. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had Kinanah ibn al-Rabi' brought, and he had the treasure of Banu al-Nadir with him. He asked him about it, and he denied that he knew its location. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought a Jewish man, who said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I have seen Kinanah go around this ruin every morning." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Kinanah: "Do you see? If we find it with you, shall we kill you?" He said: "Yes." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the ruin to be dug up, and some of their treasure was taken out. Then he asked him about the rest, but he refused to hand it over. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, saying: "Torture him until you exhaust what he has." Al-Zubayr would strike a flint against his chest until he was near death. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) handed him over to Muhammad ibn Maslamah, who struck his neck, in revenge for his brother Mahmud ibn Maslamah. [[See: Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah: 2/336 onwards, on the Battle of Khaybar.]]

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, who said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attacked Khaybar. We prayed the dawn prayer near it while it was still dark, and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) mounted, Abu Talhah mounted, and I was riding behind Abu Talhah. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) advanced into the alleys of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ). Then his lower garment was raised from his thigh until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ). When he entered the town, he said: "Allahu Akbar, Khaybar is ruined! Indeed, when we descend into the courtyard of a people, the morning of those who were warned is evil." He said it three times. The people went out to their work and said: "Muhammad!" — Abd al-Aziz said: and some of our companions said: "and the army" (al-khamis), meaning the army. He said: So we conquered it by force, and he gathered the captives. Dihyah came and said: "O Prophet of Allah, give me a slave girl from among the captives." He said: "Go and take a slave girl," and he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy. A man came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of Allah, you gave Dihyah Safiyyah bint Huyayy, the lady of Qurayzah and al-Nadir, who is fit only for you." He said: "Call him to her," so he came with her. When the Prophet (ﷺ) looked at her, he said: "Take a slave girl from the captives other than her." He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) freed her and married her. Thabit said to him: "O Abu Hamzah, what was her dowry?" He said: "Herself. He freed her and married her." When they were on the road, Umm Sulaym prepared her for him, and she presented her to him at night. So in the morning the Prophet (ﷺ) was a bridegroom. He said: "Whoever has anything, let him bring it." He spread out a leather mat, and a man came with dates, and another came with butter. [The narrator said:] I think he also mentioned sawiq (roasted barley flour). He said: They mixed it into hays (a dish of dates, butter and flour), and that was the wedding feast (walimah) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Salah, chapter: What is mentioned about the thigh: 1/479-480; and Muslim in al-Nikah, chapter: The virtue of freeing one's slave woman and then marrying her, no. (1365): 2/1042-1044.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verses 19–20 (part 2 of 2):

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi related to us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us; Musa ibn Isma'il related to us; Abd al-Wahid al-Shaybani related to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Awfa say: "We suffered a famine during the nights of Khaybar. Then, on the day of Khaybar, we fell upon the domestic donkeys and slaughtered them. When the cooking pots were boiling, the herald of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out: 'Overturn the pots, and do not eat any of the flesh of the donkeys.' Abd Allah said: We said, 'The Prophet ﷺ only forbade it because it had not been divided (khumus).' Others said, 'He forbade it absolutely.' I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he said, 'He forbade it absolutely.'" [Related by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of Khaybar: 7/481.]

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir related to us; Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad related to us; Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi related to us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us; Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us; Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi related to us; Khalid ibn al-Harith related to us; Shu'ba related to us, from Hisham ibn Zayd, from Anas: that a Jewish woman brought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a poisoned sheep, and he ate from it. Then she was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked her about that. She said, "I wanted to kill you." He said: "Allah would not have given you power over that," or he said, "over me." They said, "Shall we not kill her?" He said, "No." Anas said: "I continued to recognize it on the palate of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [Related by al-Bukhari in al-Hibah, chapter on accepting gifts from polytheists: 5/230, and by Muslim in al-Salam, chapter on poison, no. (2190): 4/1721.]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verses 19–20 (part 1 of 2)**

﴿And many spoils that they will take﴾ from the properties of the Jews of Khaybar. Khaybar had land and property, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided them among them. ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾.

﴿Allah has promised you many spoils that you will take﴾: these are the conquests that will be opened for them until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So He hastened this for you﴾, meaning Khaybar, ﴿and restrained the hands of the people from you﴾. This is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) headed for Khaybar and besieged its people, some tribes of Banu Asad and Ghatafan intended to raid the dependants and children of the Muslims in Madinah. So Allah restrained their hands by casting terror into their hearts. It was also said: "He restrained the hands of the people from you", meaning the people of Makkah, through the treaty. ﴿And that it may be a sign for the believers﴾, concerning the truthfulness of you [the Prophet], ﴿and that they may know that Allah is the One who protects and guards them, in their presence and in their absence﴾, ﴿and guides you to a straight path﴾: He will keep you firm upon Islam and increase you in insight and certainty through the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Khaybar. This is because when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyah, he remained in Madinah for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah and part of Muharram. Then he set out in the latter part of Muharram of the seventh year (AH) towards Khaybar.

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: we were informed by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us, who said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (ﷺ) : whenever he raided a people with us, he would not attack us until morning and would look. If he heard the adhan, he would refrain from them; and if he did not hear the adhan, he would attack them. He said: So we set out for Khaybar and reached them at night. When it was morning and he did not hear the adhan, he mounted, and I mounted behind Abu Talhah, and my foot was touching the foot of the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: So they came out to us with their baskets and their shovels. When they saw the Prophet (ﷺ), they said: "Muhammad, by Allah, Muhammad and the army!" When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them, he said: "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Khaybar is ruined! Indeed, when we descend into the courtyard of a people, the morning of those who were warned is evil." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter: What blood is protected by the adhan: 2/89-90; Muslim in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter on the Battle of Khaybar, no. (1365): 3/1426-1427; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/58-59.]]

We were informed by Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir, who said: we were informed by Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, who said: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us, who said: Abu Ali al-Hanafi Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Majid informed us, who said: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, who said: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to me, saying: ... We set out to Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: My uncle Amir began chanting verses to the people:

"By Allah, were it not for Allah, we would not have been guided, nor would we have given charity or prayed.
And we are not free from Your bounty, so make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy].
And send down tranquillity upon us."

[The words within the brackets are an addition from manuscript "b".]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am Amir." He said: "May your Lord forgive you." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never asked forgiveness for a person in particular except that he was martyred. He said: Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, who was on his camel, called out: "O Prophet of Allah, if only you had let us enjoy Amir!" He said: When we arrived at Khaybar, their king Marhab came out swaggering with his sword, saying: "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab, armed and a tested champion, when wars approach, blazing." [The word "Khaybar" is missing from manuscript "a".]

He said: Then my uncle Amir came out to face him and said: "Khaybar knows that I am Amir, armed and a daring champion." He said: They exchanged two blows. Marhab's sword struck the shield of Amir, and Amir went to strike from below, but his sword turned back upon himself and severed his artery, and that was the cause of his death. Salamah said: I went out and found a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) [manuscript "b" page 130] saying: "The deed of Amir has come to nothing; he killed himself." He said: So I went to the Prophet (ﷺ) weeping and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the deed of Amir has come to nothing; he killed himself." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who said that?" I said: "Some people among your companions." He said: "The one who said that has lied; rather, he will have his reward twice." Then he sent me to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who had an eye infection, and said: "I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." He said: So I went to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) and brought him, leading him by the hand while he had an eye infection, until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He spat into his eyes and they were healed, and he gave him the banner. Marhab came out saying: "Khaybar knows that I am Marhab, armed and a tested champion, when wars approach, blazing."

Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I am the one whom my mother named Haydar, like a lion of thickets, of fearsome appearance. I give them full measure with the sa', like the measuring of the sandara." [In manuscript "b": "severe, a lion" (shadid qaswarah).]

He said: So he struck the head of Marhab and killed him. Then the conquest came at his hands. [[Narrated by Muslim in extended form in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter on the Battle of Dhi Qarad, no. (1807): 3/1433-1441; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/19-22.]]

The account of Khaybar was narrated by a group: Sahl ibn Sa'd, Anas, and Abu Hurayrah, who add and omit [details from one another]. In it: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been seized by a severe headache (al-shaqiqah) and did not go out to the people. So Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) took the banner of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then advanced and fought a fierce battle, then returned. Then Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) took it and fought a fierce battle, more severe than the first, then returned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of this and said: "Tomorrow I will surely give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love; Allah will grant the conquest at his hands." He called Ali ibn Abi Talib and gave it to him, and said: "Go, and do not turn around until Allah grants you victory." So he came to the city of Khaybar, and Marhab, the lord of the fortress, came out wearing a helmet and a stone with a hole in it like a helmet upon his head, reciting verses. Ali came out to face him and struck him, splitting the stone and the helmet and cleaving his head until the sword reached the molars. Then after Marhab, his brother Yasir came out reciting verses, and al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam came out against him. His mother Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib said: "Will my son be killed, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Rather, your son will kill him, if Allah wills." Then they met, and al-Zubayr killed him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to conquer the fortresses, to kill the fighting men, to take the children captive, and to seize the wealth.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The first of their fortresses to be conquered was the fortress of Na'im, and there Mahmud ibn Maslamah was killed; the Jews threw a stone at him and killed him. Then [the Muslims] conquered al-'Amus, the fortress of Ibn Abi al-Huqayq, and obtained captives from it, among them Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab. Bilal brought her and another woman with her, and he passed by them over the corpses of Jewish men slain. When the woman with Safiyyah saw them, she screamed, struck her face, and threw dust upon her head. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw her, he said: "Take this she-devil away from me," and he ordered Safiyyah to be brought and placed behind him, and he threw his cloak over her. The Muslims knew that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had chosen her for himself. The Messenger of Allah said to Bilal, when he had seen what he had seen from that Jewish woman: "Has mercy been removed from you, O Bilal, that you pass by two women over the corpses of their men?" Safiyyah had seen in a dream, while she was a bride of Kinanah ibn al-Rabi' ibn Abi al-Huqayq, that a moon had fallen into her lap. She related her dream to her husband, and he said: "This is nothing but that you desire the king of Hijaz, Muhammad." He struck her face, and her eye turned green from it. She was brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a mark from it, and he asked her what it was. She informed him of this account. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had Kinanah ibn al-Rabi' brought, and he had the treasure of Banu al-Nadir with him. He asked him about it, and he denied that he knew its location. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought a Jewish man, who said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I have seen Kinanah go around this ruin every morning." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Kinanah: "Do you see? If we find it with you, shall we kill you?" He said: "Yes." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered the ruin to be dug up, and some of their treasure was taken out. Then he asked him about the rest, but he refused to hand it over. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, saying: "Torture him until you exhaust what he has." Al-Zubayr would strike a flint against his chest until he was near death. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) handed him over to Muhammad ibn Maslamah, who struck his neck, in revenge for his brother Mahmud ibn Maslamah. Indeed, when we descend into the courtyard of a people, the morning of those who were warned is evil." He said it three times. The people went out to their work and said: "Muhammad!" — Abd al-Aziz said: and some of our companions said: "and the army" (al-khamis), meaning the army. He said: So we conquered it by force, and he gathered the captives. Dihyah came and said: "O Prophet of Allah, give me a slave girl from among the captives." [The narrator said:] I think he also mentioned sawiq (roasted barley flour). He said: They mixed it into hays (a dish of dates, butter and flour), and that was the wedding feast (walimah) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Salah, chapter: What is mentioned about the thigh: 1/479-480; and Muslim in al-Nikah, chapter: The virtue of freeing one's slave woman and then marrying her, no. (1365): 2/1042-1044.]]

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 48, verses 21–24:**

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And another [victory] that you were not capable of [achieving]﴾, meaning: Allah promised you the conquest of another city that you were not capable of [conquering]. ﴿Allah has encompassed it﴾, meaning [He has kept it] until He grants it to you, as if He had preserved it for you and prevented others from it until you take it. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah knew that He would grant it to you.

The scholars differed concerning it. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan and Muqatil said: it refers to Persia (Fars) and the Byzantines (al-Rum). The Arabs were not capable of fighting Persia and the Byzantines; rather, they were subject to them, until they gained power over them through Islam.

al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: it refers to Khaybar. Allah promised it to His Prophet (ﷺ) before he obtained it, and they had not been expecting it.

Qatadah said: it refers to Makkah. 'Ikrimah said: it refers to Hunayn. Mujahid said: it refers to what they had not conquered until that day.

﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Competent﴾.

﴿And if those who disbelieved had fought you﴾, meaning: Asad, Ghatafan and the people of Khaybar, ﴿they would have turned their backs﴾ [would have been routed] [[Addition from manuscript "A".]], ﴿then they would not have found any ally or helper﴾.

﴿The established way of Allah which has already occurred before﴾, meaning: as is Allah's way in granting victory to His allies and subduing His enemies. ﴿And you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾.

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within [the valley of] Makkah after He had given you victory over them. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing﴾. Abu 'Amr read *ya'malun* (with the *ya'*, the third person, "they do") and the others read *ta'malun* (with the *ta'*, the second person, "you do"). The scholars differed concerning these [verses]. Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us [131/b], 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), that: eighty men from the people of Makkah came down upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the mountain of al-Tan'im, armed, intending to betray the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions. He (ﷺ) took them alive and spared them, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse: "And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within [the valley of] Makkah after He had given you victory over them." [[Narrated by Muslim in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the saying of Allah "And it is He who withheld their hands from you" to the end of the verse, no. (1808): 3/1442.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) at al-Hudaybiyah, at the foot of the tree which Allah mentions in the Qur'an, and on his back was a branch from the branches of that tree, which I lifted from his back.
