He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It is they who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque﴾ [48:25], to the end of the verse. Al-Zuhri narrated from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ left Madinah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah with more than fourteen hundred of his Companions, intending to visit the House (the Ka'bah), not intending fighting. He took with him seventy camels for sacrifice (budn, sing. badanah, a large camel offered as a sacrificial animal), and the people numbered seven hundred men, and each camel was for ten persons. When he reached Dhu al-Hulayfah, he garlanded the offering animals and marked them, and he entered the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for the 'umrah (minor pilgrimage) from there. He sent a scout of his from Khuza'ah to inform him about the Quraysh. The Prophet ﷺ continued on until he reached the pool of al-Ashtat, near 'Usfan. There 'Aynah al-Khuza'i came to him and said: "The Quraysh have gathered large forces against you, and they have gathered the Ahabish for you, and they will fight you and bar you from the House." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Advise me, O people. Do you think I should turn against the offspring of those who aided them, and seize them? If they remain seated, they will remain seated as those who have been bereaved, and if they escape, it will be a neck that Allah has cut off. Or do you think we should head for the House, and whoever bars us from it, we fight him?"

Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, you came out intending only this House, not wishing to fight anyone or to wage war. So proceed toward it, and whoever bars us from it, we will fight him."

He said: "Proceed in the name of Allah." So they set out. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with cavalry of the Quraysh as a vanguard, so take the right-hand way." By Allah, Khalid did not perceive them until suddenly he saw the dust cloud of the army, so he set off galloping to warn the Quraysh. The Prophet ﷺ continued until, when he was at the mountain pass by which they would descend upon them, his she-camel knelt down with him. The people said: "Halt, halt!" But she persisted, so they said: "al-Qaswa' has become stubborn!" The Prophet ﷺ said: "al-Qaswa' has not become stubborn, nor is that her habit, but the One who stopped the Elephant has stopped her." Then he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, the Quraysh will not ask me today for any arrangement in which they honour the sacred things of Allah, and in which there is the keeping of kinship ties, except that I will grant it to them." Then he urged her on, and she sprang up.

He said: So he turned aside from them until he halted at the farthest part of al-Hudaybiyah, at a spring of little water, which the people drew from in trickles. The people soon drained it, and they complained to the Prophet ﷺ of thirst. So he drew an arrow from his quiver and gave it to a man of his Companions called Najiyah ibn 'Umayr, who was the driver of the Prophet's ﷺ camels. He went down into the well and planted it in its bed, and by Allah, the water continued to gush forth for them until they departed from it. While they were in that state, Budayl ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i came to him with a group of his people. Khuza'ah were the trusted confidants (ʿaybat nuṣḥ, lit. the repository of sincere counsel) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among the people of Tihamah. He said: "I have left Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, who have camped at the water sources of al-Hudaybiyah, with them the milch camels with their young, and they will fight you and bar you from the House."

The Prophet ﷺ said: "We have not come to fight anyone, but we have come as pilgrims for 'umrah. The Quraysh have been worn down by war and it has harmed them. If they wish, I will make a truce with them for a period, and they leave me and the people free; if I prevail, then if they wish to enter into what the people have entered into, they may do so; otherwise they will have been shorn of strength. If they refuse, then by He in whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this affair of mine until my neck is separated, or Allah will make His command prevail."

Budayl said: "I will convey to them what you say." So he set out until he came to the Quraysh and said: "We have come to you from this man, and we heard him say a statement. If you wish, we will present it to you." Their foolish ones said: "We have no need for you to tell us anything about him." But one of their men of judgement said: "Relate what you heard him say." He said: "I heard him say such and such," and he related to them what the Prophet ﷺ had said.

Then 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi stood and said: "O people, are you not the father?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Am I not the son?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Do you suspect me?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you not know that I called out to the people of 'Ukaz, and when they refused me, I came to you with my family, my children, and whoever obeyed me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed, this man has presented you with a proposal of right guidance, so accept it, and let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." So he came to him and began speaking with the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ spoke to him similarly to what he had said to Budayl. 'Urwah then said: "O Muhammad, what do you think? If you uproot your own people, have you ever heard of any Arab who destroyed his own kin before you? And if the other outcome occurs, then by Allah, I see faces and rabble of people who are likely to flee and abandon you."

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said to him: "Suck the clitoris of al-Lat!" (al-Bazr: with a fatha on the bā' and sukūn on the mīm, a piece that remains after circumcision in a woman's genitalia; al-Lat: the name of one of the idols that the Quraysh and Thaqif worshipped. It was the custom of the Arabs to curse with this, but with the mention of the mother.) "Would we flee from him and abandon him?"

'Urwah said: "Who is this?" They said: "Abu Bakr." He said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, were it not for a favour you once did for me, which I have not yet repaid, I would have answered you."

He said: And he continued speaking with the Prophet ﷺ, and every time he spoke, he would take hold of his beard. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah was standing over the head of the Prophet ﷺ with a sword and wearing a helmet. Whenever 'Urwah reached out his hand toward the beard of the Prophet ﷺ, he would strike his hand with the scabbard of the sword and say: "Keep your hand away from the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" 'Urwah raised his head and said: "Who is this?" They said: "al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah." He said: "O treacherous one! Am I not striving to atone for your treachery?"

Al-Mughirah had accompanied a group of people in the pre-Islamic period, killed them, and taken their wealth, then came and embraced Islam. The Prophet ﷺ said: "As for Islam, I accept it; as for the wealth, I have no share in it at all."

Then 'Urwah began to observe the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never spat a spittle but it fell into the palm of one of them, and he rubbed it over his face and skin. If he ordered them, they rushed to carry out his command; if he performed ablution, they nearly fought over his ablution water; and if he spoke, they lowered their voices in his presence, and they did not fix their gaze upon him out of reverence for him." 'Urwah returned to his companions and said: "O people, by Allah, I have visited kings. I have visited Caesar, Chosroes and the Negus. By Allah, I have never seen a king whom his companions honour as the Companions of Muhammad honour Muhammad. By Allah, if he spits a spittle, it falls into the palm of one of them, and he rubs it over his face and skin. If he orders them, they rush to carry out his command; if he performs ablution, they nearly fight over his ablution water; if he speaks, they lower their voices in his presence, and they do not fix their gaze upon him out of reverence for him. Indeed, he has presented you with a proposal of right guidance, so accept it."

A man from the Banu Kinanah said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is so-and-so, and he is from a people who honour the camel offerings, so send them to him." The offerings were sent to him, and the people came out to meet him, chanting the talbiyah. When he saw that, he said: "Glory be to Allah! It is not fitting for these people to be barred from the House!"

When he returned to his companions, he said: "I have seen the camel offerings garlanded and marked, so I do not think they should be barred from the House."

Then they sent al-Hulays ibn 'Alqamah to him, and he was on that day the chief of the Ahabish. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: "This man is from a people who venerate God, so send the offerings before him so that he may see them." When he saw the offerings flowing toward him from the side of the valley, garlanded, their wool worn away from the long detention, he returned to the Quraysh without reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, out of awe at what he had seen. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh, I have seen what is not lawful: offerings barred from their place, garlanded, their wool worn away from long detention." They said to him: "Sit down; you are only a bedouin with no knowledge." Al-Hulays became angry at that and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, we did not form our alliance with you on this basis, nor did we make our pact with you on this basis: that you bar from the House of Allah those who come to it honouring it! By He in whose hand is the soul of al-Hulays, you will either allow Muhammad and what he came for to proceed, or I will bring out the Ahabish in one single outburst." They said to him: "Enough! Hold back from us, O Hulays, until we take for ourselves what we are content with."

A man from them called Mikraz ibn Hafs stood up and said: "Let me go to him." They said: "Go to him." When he came in sight of them, the Prophet ﷺ said: "This is Mikraz, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Prophet ﷺ, and while he was speaking with him, Suhayl ibn 'Amr came. 'Ikrimah said: When the Prophet ﷺ saw him, he said: "Your affair has been made easy for you."

Al-Zuhri said in his narration: Suhayl ibn 'Amr came and said: "Come, let us write a document between us and you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and said to him: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

Suhayl said: "As for al-Rahman, by Allah, I do not know what it is. Rather, write: In Your name, O Allah, as you used to write."

The Muslims said: "By Allah, we will not write it except: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."

The Prophet ﷺ said to 'Ali: "Write: In Your name, O Allah." Then he said: "Write: This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed upon."

Suhayl said: "By Allah, if we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have barred you from the House nor fought you. Rather, write: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. Write, O 'Ali: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah."

Al-Zuhri said: This was in accordance with His saying: ﴿They do not ask for any arrangement in which they honour the sacred things of Allah, but I will grant it to them﴾. So he wrote: "This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has settled with Suhayl ibn 'Amr." They agreed to suspend war among the people for ten years, during which people would be safe and some would refrain from others. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "And on condition that you let us reach the House, so that we may circumambulate it." Suhayl said: "By Allah, the Arabs must not say that we were coerced; rather, that will be in the coming year." So it was written. Suhayl said: "And on condition that no man from us comes to you, even if he is upon your religion, except that you return him to us." The Muslims said: "Glory be to Allah! How can he be returned to the polytheists when he has come as a Muslim?"

Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Bara' the story of the treaty, and in it they said: "If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have prevented you from anything, but you are Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah." He said: "I am the Messenger of Allah and I am Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah." Then he said to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Erase 'Messenger of Allah'." He said: "No, by Allah, I will never erase it." He said: "Then show it to me." So he showed it to him, and the Prophet ﷺ erased it with his own hand. In another narration: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the document, though he could not write well, and wrote: "This is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah has settled."

Al-Bara' said: He concluded the treaty on three matters: that whoever came to him from the polytheists he would return to them, and whoever came to them from the Muslims they would not return; that he would enter it (Makkah) in the following year and stay there for three days; and that he would not enter it except with light weapons in their sheaths, such as the sword, the bow, and the like.

Ṯābit reported from Anas that the Quraysh made a treaty with the Prophet ﷺ and stipulated that whoever came to them from among the Muslims, they would not return to the Muslims, and whoever came to the Muslims from among them, the Muslims would return to them. They said, "O Messenger of God, shall we write this down?" He said, "Yes. Whoever among us goes to them, God will keep far from him, and whoever comes to us from them, God will make for him a way out and a relief."

We return to the hadith of al-Zuhri, who said: While they were in that state, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came, dragging himself in his shackles. He had escaped and come out from the lower part of Mecca, until he threw himself among the Muslims. Suhayl said, "O Muhammad, this is the first man I demand you return to me under the terms of the agreement." The Prophet said, "We have not yet finalized the document." Suhayl said, "By God, then I will never make a settlement with you on any terms." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Then grant him protection for me." He said, "I will not grant it to you." He said, "Yes, do so." He said, "I will not do it." Then Suhayl began dragging him to return him to Quraysh. Abu Jandal cried out, "O assembly of Muslims, am I to be returned to the polytheists when I have come as a Muslim? Do you not see what I have suffered?" He had been subjected to severe torture for the sake of God.

In the hadith it is also related that the Messenger of God ﷺ said, "O Abu Jandal, be patient and seek reward, for God will make for you and for those with you among the oppressed a relief and a way out. We have indeed concluded a covenant and a treaty between us and these people, and we will not betray them." Then ʿUmar leapt up and walked beside Abu Jandal, saying, "Be patient, for they are only polytheists, and the blood of one of them is like the blood of a dog," and he brought the hilt of a sword close to him. ʿUmar said, "I hoped he would take the sword and strike his father with it, but the man was reluctant regarding his father."

The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ had set out, not doubting the conquest, because of a dream the Messenger of God ﷺ had seen. When they saw this, a great distress came over the people, to the point that they nearly perished, and the matter of Abu Jandal increased their evil state.

ʿUmar said: "By God, I have had no doubt since I embraced Islam except on that day."

Al-Zuhri said in his hadith, from ʿUrwah, from Marwan and al-Miswar. Abu Wa'il also narrated it from Sahl ibn Ḥunayf. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, 'Are you not truly the Prophet of God?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Are we not upon the truth while our enemy is upon falsehood?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Are not our slain in Paradise and their slain in Hell?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?' He said, 'I am the Messenger of God and I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper.' I said, 'Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said, 'Yes. But did I tell you that we would come to it this year?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

He said: "Then I went to Abu Bakr and said, 'O Abu Bakr, is this not truly the Prophet of God?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Are we not upon the truth while our enemy is upon falsehood?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Are not our slain in Paradise and their slain in Hell?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?' He said, 'O man, he is the Messenger of God; he does not disobey his Lord, and his Lord is his helper. So hold fast to his stirrup, for by God he is upon the truth.' I said, 'Did he not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?' He said, 'Yes. But did he inform you that you would come to it this year?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Then you will come to it and circumambulate it.'"

Al-Zuhri said: ʿUmar said, "Because of that, I did many good deeds (to atone for it)."

He said: When the Prophet ﷺ had finished with the matter of the document, he said to his Companions, "Arise, sacrifice, then shave your heads." He said: By God, not one man among them got up, even after he said it three times. When none of them rose, he went in to Umm Salamah and told her what he had encountered from the people. Umm Salamah said, "O Prophet of God, do you wish for this? Go out, and do not speak a single word to any of them until you sacrifice your camel and call your barber so he may shave you." So he went out and did not speak to anyone until he had done that: he sacrificed his camel and called his barber, who shaved him. When they saw that, they rose and sacrificed, and some of them began shaving others, until some of them nearly killed one another out of grief.

Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas said: "On the day of al-Ḥudaybiyah, some men shaved their heads and others trimmed their hair. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, 'May God have mercy on those who shaved.' They said, 'And those who trimmed?' He said, 'May God have mercy on those who shaved.' They said, 'O Messenger of God, and those who trimmed?' He said, 'And those who trimmed.' They said, 'O Messenger of God, why did you especially emphasize mercy for those who shaved rather than those who trimmed?' He said, 'Because they did not doubt.'" Ibn ʿUmar said: "That was because some people hesitated and said, 'Perhaps we will circumambulate the House.'"

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "On the year of al-Ḥudaybiyah, the Messenger of God ﷺ gave among his sacrificial animals a camel belonging to Abu Jahl, which had a silver ring in its nose, in order to enrage the polytheists with that."

Al-Zuhri said in his hadith: "Then believing women came to him, and God the Exalted revealed, ﴿O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants﴾, until He reached 'the disbelieving women' (Q. 60:10). On that day ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, divorced two women who had been his wives while they were polytheists. Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married one of them, and Safwan ibn Umayyah married the other." He said: "He forbade them to return the women and ordered the return of the bride-price."

He said: "Then the Prophet ﷺ returned to Medina, and there came to him Abu Basir ʿUtbah ibn Usayd, a man of Quraysh who was a Muslim, and who had been among those detained in Mecca. Azhar ibn ʿAbd ʿAwf and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi wrote concerning him to the Messenger of God ﷺ and sent a man from the Banu ʿAmir ibn Lu'ayy, together with a client of theirs, in pursuit of him. The two of them came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, 'The covenant that you made for us.' The Messenger of God ﷺ said, 'O Abu Basir, we have given these people what you know, and betrayal is not permissible in our religion. God will make for you and for those with you among the oppressed a relief and a way out.' Then he handed him over to the two men, and they went out with him until they reached Dhu al-Ḥulayfah, where they alighted and ate some of their dates. Abu Basir said to one of the two men, 'By God, I see that your sword is fine.' The other drew it and said, 'Yes, by God, it is very fine. I have tested it, and tested it again.' Abu Basir said, 'Show me, so that I may look at it.' They gave it to him, and he struck him with it until he died. The other fled until he reached Medina and entered the mosque running. When the Messenger of God ﷺ saw him, he said, 'This man has seen something alarming.' When he reached the Prophet ﷺ, he said, 'Woe to you, what is the matter with you?' He said, 'By God, my companion has been killed, and I am about to be killed.' Then Abu Basir came, by God, not long after, carrying his sword over his shoulder, until he stood before the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, 'O Prophet of God, may God fulfil your covenant! You returned me to them, and then God delivered me from them.' The Prophet ﷺ said, 'Woe to his mother! He is a warlike man (mis'ar ḥarb). If only he had someone with him!' When he heard that, he realized that he would return him to them. So he went out until he reached the coast (Sayf al-Baḥr). The Muslims who had been detained in Mecca learned of the Prophet's ﷺ words to Abu Basir, 'Woe to his mother, he is a warlike man; if only he had someone with him.' So a band of them went out to him, and Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl escaped and joined Abu Basir, until nearly seventy men gathered with him. By God, they did not hear of any caravan leaving Quraysh for Syria without intercepting it, killing its people and taking their property. So Quraysh sent to the Prophet ﷺ, appealing to him by God and by kinship to send for them, and whoever came to him would be safe. The Prophet ﷺ sent for them, and they came to him in Medina. Then God the Exalted revealed: ﴿And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca, after He had given you victory over them. And God is ever Seeing of what you do﴾ (Q. 48:24), until He reached 'the zealotry of ignorance.' Their zealotry was that they did not acknowledge that he was the Prophet of God ﷺ, nor did they acknowledge 'In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate' (al-basmala), and they barred him from the House."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in the chapter on conditions, "What is permissible of conditions in Islam," 5/312, and at length in the chapter on conditions in jihad and reconciliation with the people of war and the writing of conditions, 5/329–333. See also Fath al-Bari, 5/333 and following.]]

God the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿They are the ones who disbelieved﴾, meaning the disbelievers of Mecca. ﴿And barred you from al-Masjid al-Ḥaram﴾ from circumambulating it. ﴿And the sacrificial animals﴾, meaning they barred the sacrificial animals (hadi), which are the camels that the Messenger of God ﷺ had driven, and there were seventy camels. ﴿Detained﴾, meaning held back. It is said: "I detained him, detaining him (ʿakfan), when I held him back," and ʿukūfan is an intransitive form, just as it is said "he returned (rajaʿa) a returning (rajʿan) and a return (rujūʿan)." ﴿From reaching its place of sacrifice﴾, its place of slaughter, and the place where its sacrifice is lawful, meaning the sacred precinct. ﴿And were it not for believing men and believing women﴾, meaning the oppressed ones in Mecca, ﴿whom you did not know﴾, whom you did not recognize, ﴿that you might trample them﴾ by killing them and inflicting harm on them, ﴿and there would befall you because of them a ma'arrah without knowledge.' Ibn Zayd said: "Ma'arrah is sin." Ibn Ishaq said: "It is the payment of blood-money (diyah)."

It is also said: it refers to expiation (kaffarah), because God the Mighty and Majestic obligated, for one who kills a believer in the land of war when his faith is not known, expiation rather than blood-money. He said: ﴿And if he was from a people hostile to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾ (Q. 4:92).

It is also said: the ma'arrah is that the polytheists would blame you and say, "They killed their own religious people." The ma'arrah is hardship. The meaning is: were it not that you might trample believing men and believing women whom you did not know, you would be liable for them expiation or be struck by disgrace. The answer to "were it not" (lawla) is omitted, and its implied meaning is: "He would have permitted you to enter it, but He prevented that between you and it."

﴿That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills﴾. The lam in "li-yudkhila" is connected to an omitted element indicated by the meaning of the speech. The meaning is: He prevented that between you and it, so that God may admit into His mercy, into the religion of Islam, whom He wills from the people of Mecca after the treaty, before you enter it. ﴿If they had been separated﴾, if they had been distinguished, meaning the believers from the disbelievers, ﴿We would have punished those of them who disbelieved with a painful punishment﴾, by captivity and killing at your hands.

Some scholars said: "We would have punished" is the answer to two clauses: the first is "were it not for believing men," and the second is "if they had been separated." Then He said, ﴿That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills﴾, meaning the believing men and believing women.

And His saying, ﴿into His mercy﴾, means His Paradise. Qatadah said regarding this verse: "God wards off the disbelievers by means of the believers, just as He warded off the oppressed believers from the polytheists of Mecca."

When the disbelievers instilled in their hearts zealotry (ḥamiyyah), at the time they barred the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions from the House, and did not acknowledge "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," and denied that Muhammad was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Al-ḥamiyyah means al-anafah (disdain, pride), as one says: "So-and-so is dhū ḥamiyyah" when he is one of anger and disdain.

Muqatil said: The people of Makkah said: "They killed our sons and our brothers, and then they enter upon us, [so the Arabs will say that they entered upon us]" [[The words between the brackets are omitted from manuscript "A".]] "in spite of us! By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, they will not enter it upon us!" So this is "the zealotry of the Jahiliyyah" that entered their hearts.

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers﴾, so that there did not enter them what had entered them of zealotry, whereby they would disobey Allah in fighting them. ﴿And He made them adhere to the word of piety﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, 'Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and most of the exegetes said: the word of piety is "There is no god but Allah" [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/536-537.]].

It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

'Ali and Ibn 'Umar said: "The word of piety" is "There is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest" [[Related by al-Tabari: 26/104; see also al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/99.]].

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: It is "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is over all things competent" [[Related by al-Tabari: 26/105; see also al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/99.]].

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah" [[Related by al-Tabari: 26/106.]].

Al-Zuhri said: It is "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate" [[Related by al-Tabari: 26/106, and 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Tafsir: 2/229; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/537 also attributes it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]].

﴿And they were more deserving of it﴾ than the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿and worthy of it﴾; that is, they were its people in the knowledge of Allah, because Allah the Exalted chose for His religion and for the companionship of His Prophet the people of goodness. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verse 27:

﴿Indeed, Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision with truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security.﴾ This was because the Prophet (ﷺ) was shown in a dream in Medina, before he set out for al-Hudaybiyah, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred Mosque in security, shaving their heads and cutting their hair short. He told his companions of this, and they rejoiced and thought that they would enter Makkah that same year. When they turned back without having entered, it grieved them, and so Allah revealed this verse [[See: al-Tabari: 26/107; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/538.]].

It is related from Majma' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari that he said: "We witnessed al-Hudaybiyah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [When we turned back from it, we saw people shaking their camels. Some of them said: 'What is the matter with the people?' They said: 'Revelation has come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So we set out hurrying, and we found the Prophet (ﷺ)] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] standing on his mount at Kura' al-Ghamim. When the people gathered around him, he recited: 'Indeed, We have given you a clear victory.' Umar said: 'Is it a victory, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand my soul is.'" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter: On one to whom a share is assigned: 2/52-53; and by Imam Ahmad: 3/420; and by al-Hakim: 2/131, who said: "Its chain is sound, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]]

In this there is evidence that what is meant by the victory is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, and that the fulfilment of the vision occurred in the following year. Then He, exalted is His remembrance, said:

"Allah fulfilled for His Messenger the vision with truth," meaning: He informed that the vision which He showed him when he set out to al-Hudaybiyah, that he and his companions would enter the Sacred Mosque, is true and real.

His saying: ﴿you will surely enter﴾ means "He said: you will surely enter." Ibn Kaysan said: "you will surely enter" is part of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to his companions, relating his vision. Allah then informed about His Messenger that he said that. He made the exception ("if Allah wills"), though he knew that they would enter by Allah's informing him, in order to observe the etiquette taught by Allah, since He said to him: "And never say of anything, 'Indeed, I will do that tomorrow,' except [with the qualification], 'If Allah wills'" [Al-Kahf: 23].

Abu Ubaydah said: "in" ("if") here means "when" ("idh"), its meaning being: "when Allah wills," as in His saying: "if you are believers" [meaning: since you are believers].

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: It is possible that the exception applies to the entering, because between the vision and its fulfilment there was a year, and some people died during that year. So the meaning of the verse is: "You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, all of you, if Allah wills."

It has also been said that the exception applies to the security, not to the entering, because there was no doubt about the entering. This is like the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) when entering the graveyard: "And indeed we, if Allah wills, will join you" [[A portion of a hadith narrated by Muslim in al-Janaiz, chapter: What is said upon entering the graves and supplicating for their people, no. (975): 2/671.]]. So the exception refers to the joining, not to the death.

﴿shaving your heads﴾ entirely, ﴿and cutting short﴾ by taking some of the hair. ﴿You did not fear, so He knew what you did not know﴾, that the good lay in the treaty and in delaying the entry. This is His saying: ﴿And if not for believing men and believing women﴾ up to the verse [Al-Fath: 25].

﴿Then He placed before that﴾, meaning: before your entering the Sacred Mosque, ﴿a near victory﴾, which, according to most scholars, is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. It has also been said that it is the conquest of Khaybar.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verse 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion; and sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾ That is, as a witness that you are a truthful Prophet in what you report.

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.﴾ The speech ends here, as related from Ibn 'Abbas; He bore witness to him with the prophethood. Then He said, beginning anew: ﴿And those who are with him﴾. The waw in it is for resumption (isti'naf), meaning: and those who are with him from among the believers. ﴿Are severe against the disbelievers﴾, harsh toward them, like a lion over its prey, showing them no mercy. ﴿Merciful among themselves﴾, affectionate and loving one another, like a child with a parent, as He said: "humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers" [Al-Ma'idah: 54]. ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾, He informs of the abundance of their prayer and their constancy in it. ﴿Seeking bounty from Allah﴾, that He admit them to Paradise, ﴿and approval﴾, that He be pleased with them. ﴿Their mark﴾, that is, their sign, ﴿is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾. The scholars differed concerning this mark. Some said: it is a light and whiteness in their faces on the Day of Resurrection by which they are recognized as having prostrated in the world; this is the narration of 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: their faces became radiant from their abundant prayer. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: the places of prostration on their faces will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.

Others said: it is the good bearing, humility, and modesty. This is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It is not what you think, but it is the sign of Islam, its disposition, its bearing, and its humility." This is also the saying of Mujahid, and the meaning is that prostration brought them humility and a good bearing by which they are recognized.

al-Dahhak said: it is the yellowness of the face from staying awake at night.

al-Hasan said: when you see them you think they are sick, but they are not sick.

'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the trace of dust on the foreheads.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: they prostrate upon the dust, not upon garments.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: everyone who keeps the five daily prayers is included in this verse. [[Al-Tabari cited these sayings (26/110-112) and then said, giving preference: "The most correct of these sayings is to say: God, exalted is He, informed us that the mark of these people whose description He gave is on their faces from the trace of prostration, and He did not restrict it to one time over another. Since that is so, it applies at all times. So their mark by which they were recognized in this world is the trace of Islam: its humility, guidance, asceticism and bearing, and the effects of performing its obligations and voluntary acts. And in the Hereafter, what He informed that they are recognized by: the blaze on the face and the whiteness on the hands and feet from the effect of ablution, and the whiteness of the faces from the effect of prostration."]]

﴿That is﴾ the description I have mentioned, ﴿their likeness﴾, their description, ﴿in the Torah﴾. Here the speech ends. Then He mentioned their description in the Gospel, saying: ﴿And their likeness﴾, their description, ﴿in the Gospel is like a seed that sends out its shoot﴾. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir recited "shat'ahu" with a fatha on the ta', while the others recited it with a sukun, and both are dialects, like "al-nahr" and "al-nahar". It means its offshoots. It is said: "ash-shara'a al-zar'u fa-huwa mushti'" when the crop puts forth its shoots. Muqatil said: it is one plant, and when what comes after it emerges, that is its shoot. al-Suddi said: it is that it brings forth with it the other shoot.

His saying: ﴿So it strengthens it﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "fa-azarahu" with a short vowel (qasr), and the rest with a long vowel (madd), meaning: it strengthened it, helped it, and supported it. ﴿Then it becomes thick﴾, that crop grew thick. ﴿So it stands firm﴾, that is, its growth was completed, became interlaced, and stood up ﴿on its stalk﴾, its roots. ﴿Pleasing the sowers﴾, that crop pleased its sowers.

This is a parable which Allah, mighty and majestic, struck in the Gospel for the companions of Muhammad ﷺ: that they would be few, then increase and multiply.

Qatadah said: the likeness of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Gospel is written: that a people will come forth who will sprout like the growth of the crop, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/114.]]

It is also said: "the crop" is Muhammad ﷺ, and "the shoot" is his companions and the believers.

It is narrated from Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, who said: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who are with him": Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him; "severe against the disbelievers": 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him; "merciful among themselves": 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him; "you see them bowing and prostrating": 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him; "seeking bounty from Allah": the rest of the ten given the good news of Paradise.

It is also said: "like a seed": Muhammad; "that sends out its shoot": Abu Bakr; "so it strengthens it": 'Umar; "so it becomes thick": 'Uthman, for Islam; "so it stands firm on its stalk": 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Islam was made upright by his sword; "pleasing the sowers": he said: they are the believers.

﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾. The saying of 'Umar to the people of Makkah after he embraced Islam: "Do not worship Allah in secret after today."

We were told by Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Shujā'i al-Sarakhsi, by dictation: Abu Bakr 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Qaffal informed us; Abu Ahmad 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Fadl al-Samarqandi narrated to us; my shaykh Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Balkhi narrated to us; Abu Raja' Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us; 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Abu Bakr is in Paradise, 'Umar is in Paradise, 'Uthman is in Paradise, 'Ali is in Paradise, Talhah is in Paradise, al-Zubayr is in Paradise, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf is in Paradise, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is in Paradise, Sa'id ibn Zayd is in Paradise, and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah is in Paradise." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib, Manaqib 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf: 10/249, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd from his father from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. It is also narrated by him (10/249) through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd from his father from Sa'id ibn Zayd, and he said: this is more sound than the first. Imam Ahmad in Fada'il al-Sahabah: 1/278 with a good chain; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/128.]]

We were told by Abu al-Muzaffar Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tamimi: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman ibn Qasim informed us; Khaythamah ibn Sulayman ibn Haydarah al-Atrabulusi narrated to us; Ahmad ibn Hashim al-Antaki narrated to us; Qutbah ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us; Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The most merciful of my community is Abu Bakr, the most firm in the matter of Allah is 'Umar, the most truthful in modesty is 'Uthman, the best in inheritance law is Zayd, the best reciter is Ubayy, the most knowledgeable in the lawful and unlawful is Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and every community has a trustee, and the trustee of this community is Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in the Muqaddimah, the virtue of Khabbab, no. (154): 1/55; al-Tirmidhi indicated it saying: Abu Qilabah narrated it from Anas from the Prophet ﷺ similarly. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verses 28–29 (part 2 of 2):

Abu al-Tayyib Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ala al-Baghawi informed us: Abu Ma'mar al-Fadl ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili narrated to us: my grandfather Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili informed us: al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri informed me: al-Mufaddal ibn Ghassan ibn al-Mufaddal al-Ala'i narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us: Ubayda ibn Abi Rabita narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Allah regarding my Companions! Allah, Allah regarding my Companions! Allah, Allah regarding my Companions! Do not take them as targets after me. Whoever loves them, it is out of love for me that he loves them; and whoever hates them, it is out of hatred for me that he hates them. Whoever harms them has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed Allah, and whoever harms Allah, it is near that He will seize him." [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib, chapter: Whoever reviles the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): 10/365, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route." Also by Imam Ahmad: 4/87, and in Fada'il al-Sahaba 1/48–49; Ibn Hibban in al-Manaqib, no. (2284), pp. 568–569; al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 9/123; Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya: 7/287; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/70. In its chain is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad, of whom al-Dhahabi said: "He is not known." In al-Mizan: "There is disturbance (idtirab) in the hadith." See Fayd al-Qadir: 2/98.]]

Abu al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamid al-Tamimi narrated to us: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman ibn al-Qasim informed us: Abu al-Hasan Khaythama ibn Sulayman informed us: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Absi al-Qassar in Kufa narrated to us: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my Companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equal to Uhud, he would not attain a mudd of one of them, nor half of it." [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in Fada'il Ashab al-Nabi (ﷺ), chapter on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "If I were to take a close friend": 7/21; and Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahaba, chapter: The prohibition of reviling the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, no. (2540), 4/1967; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/69.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Za'farani informed us, narrating: Abu Muhammad Abd Allah ibn Urwa narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ishkab narrated to us: Shababa [[In manuscript "A": Bashara.]] ibn Sawwar narrated to us: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Abu Khabbab, from Abu Sulaym al-Hamdani, from his father, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If it pleases you to be among the people of Paradise, then indeed there are a people who pretend to love you, who recite the Qur'an but it does not go beyond their collarbones. The Rafida have nicknamed them. If you encounter them, then fight them, for they are polytheists." [[The author of Kanz al-Ummal cited it: 11/324, as attributed to Ibn Bishran and al-Hakim in al-Kuna.]] Regarding the chain of this hadith, there is scrutiny (nazar).

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward﴾. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: meaning, from the offshoot (shatA) that the seed produced, and they are those who enter Islam after the sowing until the Day of Resurrection. He returned the pronouns (the "hā'" and "mīm") to the meaning of the shatA, not to its wording; and for this reason he did not say "minhu" (from it). ﴿Forgiveness and a great reward﴾: meaning, Paradise.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 48, verse 28–29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion; and sufficient is Allah as Witness.﴾ That is, as a witness that you are a truthful Prophet in what you report.

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.﴾ The speech ends here, as related from Ibn 'Abbas; He bore witness to him with the prophethood. Then He said, beginning anew: ﴿And those who are with him﴾. The waw in it is for resumption (isti'naf), meaning: and those who are with him from among the believers. ﴿Are severe against the disbelievers﴾, harsh toward them, like a lion over its prey, showing them no mercy. ﴿Merciful among themselves﴾, affectionate and loving one another, like a child with a parent, as He said: "humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers" [Al-Ma'idah: 54]. ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating﴾, He informs of the abundance of their prayer and their constancy in it. ﴿Seeking bounty from Allah﴾, that He admit them to Paradise, ﴿and approval﴾, that He be pleased with them. ﴿Their mark﴾, that is, their sign, ﴿is on their faces from the trace of prostration﴾. The scholars differed concerning this mark. Some said: it is a light and whiteness in their faces on the Day of Resurrection by which they are recognized as having prostrated in the world; this is the narration of 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: their faces became radiant from their abundant prayer. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: the places of prostration on their faces will be like the moon on the night of the full moon.

Others said: it is the good bearing, humility, and modesty. This is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "It is not what you think, but it is the sign of Islam, its disposition, its bearing, and its humility." This is also the saying of Mujahid, and the meaning is that prostration brought them humility and a good bearing by which they are recognized.

al-Dahhak said: it is the yellowness of the face from staying awake at night.

al-Hasan said: when you see them you think they are sick, but they are not sick.

'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the trace of dust on the foreheads.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: they prostrate upon the dust, not upon garments.

'Ata' al-Khurasani said: everyone who keeps the five daily prayers is included in this verse. [[Al-Tabari cited these sayings (26/110-112) and then said, giving preference: "The most correct of these sayings is to say: God, exalted is He, informed us that the mark of these people whose description He gave is on their faces from the trace of prostration, and He did not restrict it to one time over another. Since that is so, it applies at all times. So their mark by which they were recognized in this world is the trace of Islam: its humility, guidance, asceticism and bearing, and the effects of performing its obligations and voluntary acts. And in the Hereafter, what He informed that they are recognized by: the blaze on the face and the whiteness on the hands and feet from the effect of ablution, and the whiteness of the faces from the effect of prostration."]]

﴿That is﴾ the description I have mentioned, ﴿their likeness﴾, their description, ﴿in the Torah﴾. Here the speech ends. Then He mentioned their description in the Gospel, saying: ﴿And their likeness﴾, their description, ﴿in the Gospel is like a seed that sends out its shoot﴾. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir recited "shat'ahu" with a fatha on the ta', while the others recited it with a sukun, and both are dialects, like "al-nahr" and "al-nahar". It means its offshoots. It is said: "ash-shara'a al-zar'u fa-huwa mushti'" when the crop puts forth its shoots. Muqatil said: it is one plant, and when what comes after it emerges, that is its shoot. al-Suddi said: it is that it brings forth with it the other shoot.

His saying: ﴿So it strengthens it﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "fa-azarahu" with a short vowel (qasr), and the rest with a long vowel (madd), meaning: it strengthened it, helped it, and supported it. ﴿Then it becomes thick﴾, that crop grew thick. ﴿So it stands firm﴾, that is, its growth was completed, became interlaced, and stood up ﴿on its stalk﴾, its roots. ﴿Pleasing the sowers﴾, that crop pleased its sowers.

This is a parable which Allah, mighty and majestic, struck in the Gospel for the companions of Muhammad ﷺ: that they would be few, then increase and multiply.

Qatadah said: the likeness of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Gospel is written: that a people will come forth who will sprout like the growth of the crop, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 26/114.]]

It is also said: "the crop" is Muhammad ﷺ, and "the shoot" is his companions and the believers.

It is narrated from Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, who said: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and those who are with him": Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him; "severe against the disbelievers": 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him; "merciful among themselves": 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him; "you see them bowing and prostrating": 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him; "seeking bounty from Allah": the rest of the ten given the good news of Paradise.

It is also said: "like a seed": Muhammad; "that sends out its shoot": Abu Bakr; "so it strengthens it": 'Umar; "so it becomes thick": 'Uthman, for Islam; "so it stands firm on its stalk": 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Islam was made upright by his sword; "pleasing the sowers": he said: they are the believers.

﴿That He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾. The saying of 'Umar to the people of Makkah after he embraced Islam: "Do not worship Allah in secret after today."

We were told by Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Shujā'i al-Sarakhsi, by dictation: Abu Bakr 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Qaffal informed us; Abu Ahmad 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Fadl al-Samarqandi narrated to us; my shaykh Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Balkhi narrated to us; Abu Raja' Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us; 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd, from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Abu Bakr is in Paradise, 'Umar is in Paradise, 'Uthman is in Paradise, 'Ali is in Paradise, Talhah is in Paradise, al-Zubayr is in Paradise, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf is in Paradise, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is in Paradise, Sa'id ibn Zayd is in Paradise, and Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah is in Paradise."
